about: Capture-time provenance for docs/screens/*.png (#335). One row per shot, written by the session that took the pixels: sha256/canvas are properties of the bytes, origin/install/url/seed/level/layout/sampleRate/build are properties of the instrument and cannot be recovered from the PNG afterwards. `node tools/recap.js check` verifies each row against the file it addresses and against every other row of the same (seed, level, sampleRate); the vocabulary, the route verdicts and the audio-draw rule live in tools/recap.js, not here.
plan: Shared by all six shots and recorded in README.md's capture block: window 1440x763 on the deployed build at ?dev=1&seed=60, DEV.boot(); DEV.freeze(true); DEV.tick(30), then DEV.cam(...) and one DEV.tick(1) per shot, vitals pinned at 100, the level's own hostiles cleared (never DEV.clear()), level banner taken down with banner('', 0). A frozen clock does not stop S.t, so these frames are reproducible by statistics and never by md5. **One term this plan did not record: the audio device.** A live boot advances the seeded stream through SND.init's noise buffer before the generator runs, so one seed deals one level per sample rate (#404, and the rule the tool prints as HW_WHY). These six captures read no SND.ac.sampleRate, so every row carries `sampleRate: null`, `check` prints each one as a device-scoped deal, and the binding below is per-machine: it says this frame is what ?dev=1&seed=60 dealt on the capture's audio device, not that every machine deals it. `STRICT=1 node tools/recap.js check` gates the missing term. A capture that reads the rate narrows its own row to one machine and one device. **Two more terms say which deal a url prints, and neither is missing shipped code.** (1) **One boot per page load.** The page pins the dice itself: `?dev=1&seed=<int>` installs mulberry over `Math.random` before anything generates (`js/90_dev.js:26`) and reports it as `DEV.seed` and as the `[DEV] seed <n> (mulberry)` boot line (`js/90_dev.js:500`, `:506`). The pin is installed once, at script load, so a second `DEV.boot()` inside the same page load draws from the advanced stream and deals a different level (`js/90_dev.js:21-22`) - a ROUTE rule: re-take by reloading the url, never by booting twice. Measured on the deployed build for #431, one machine, 44100 Hz: two page loads of `?dev=1&seed=60` each read level 0 as layout 3105224175 from the load-time boot, and 3547860569 both times after a second in-page `DEV.boot()`. (A `seedRng` ReferenceError is only the name of a `tools/view.js` global the page has no reason to define; it says nothing about whether the page pins the stream.) (2) **The build.** The generator's draw count moves between builds, so `layout` is a fact of the row's `build` as much as of its url: three of the `level0-*` rows still bind `735688443` from `ce9d39d`, which is why a capture taken off today's deploy disagrees with them - a stale-by-build disagreement, named per row in `staleByBuild` and printed and counted by `check`, never gated. The other two `level0-*` rows were re-taken off that deploy for #431 and bind `3105224175` at `8a8fb15`; a row's `layout` is a fact of its `build` as much as of its url, so one (seed, level) can appear twice in this table with two layouts, which `check` prints as a SPLIT note and not as a contradiction. The hand-authored level needs no such label, which is why `level3-stack` is the one row refreshed since these rows were written.

This move has ONE cause and it is small: #369 stops the finale's deck burning past the picture it is lit for, so the deck third falls 3.5 and the wall and vault do not move - a wide, shallow pixel diff, not a repaint. The previous row's 63 % >2-luma move at mean |delta| 26.6 was three changes at once; this one is 37 % at 5.2. Two page loads of this route at this build both read DEV.layoutSig() 1699332737 and canvas means 66.273 / 66.280 (in-page reads, ahead of the screenshot encode), so this pair of shutters agrees; the row this replaces recorded 972763321 and 164933889 across two loads of its own build. So this layout is a property of the url AND of the build, not of the run: the page installs the seeded dice itself from `?dev=1&seed=` (`js/90_dev.js:26`, reported as `DEV.seed` and as the `[DEV] seed 60 (mulberry)` boot line), and one page load is one deal, so a re-take reloads the url instead of booting twice (`js/90_dev.js:21-22`). The two layouts this row replaces read across its own two loads were a route that booted twice, not an unpinned stream (#431 corrected what an earlier session of #420 recorded here).  Geometry is not among the things that moved and the caption still asserts it, so it was read back off the same page at this seat: own cell 1,2 air, floor 0.00, own ceiling 1.00, MAP.cz 4, MAP.light 0.102; the seventh cell along the heading (7.28, 6.45) is air at floor 0.00 with its ceiling solving at 4.00. The same seat, same deal, same page load rules, turned to the fitting this deal puts over the entry circulation: DEV.cam(18.5, 23.5, floorAt(...), -0.556, 25). MAP.ceilPanes for this layout holds six entries and the one 3.06 m from the seat at bearing -0.556 rad is the one in this frame, hung with its lens at 2.35 m under a 4.00 m slab; MAP.ceilFix marks its cell 2 (canopy on the slab, lens on the stem), which is the tall-room form. The slab's left third is the doorway wall the seat stands in, 1 m away - it is in the picture the player sees when they turn, and it is why this frame is not a clean room shot. Same seed/level/sampleRate as level2-abatoir and the same layout 3946763407, so the two rows are one world at two headings. S.mode read 'play'; colour type 2 via tools/png_rgb.js.
